review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner, regression design self-review
review.decision: Preserve native Codex title ownership across connection lifecycle
review.notes: The independent review and an isolated run on the merged base reproduced a user rename acknowledged and read back between the bridge's empty read and unconditional write. Codex 0.171.0 exposes no atomic name-if-empty operation. The reviewed contract leaves title ownership with Codex, including on unnamed roots, and limits gtmux title projection to a verified binding on a pane stamped for this HQ. Fixtures verify frame and accessor boundaries. A separate native run verifies persisted names. Independent review is still required on the exact PR head.

cases.description: A stale unnamed root response leaves a concurrently confirmed Codex name intact
cases.setup: Initialize the configured-home observer and production forwarding over two private sockets. Hold an unnamed root response while a separate client sets and reads back a name. Use a fake server in the portable test and an isolated Codex 0.171.0 server for native verification.
cases.action: Deliver the stale root response and then the native name notification. Verify user, ordinary, and HQ traffic at the forwarding boundary.
cases.expected: The original root result and native notification reach the frontend unchanged and only ordinary root binding occurs. A fresh name read still returns the user's name, with no automatic title mutation. The obsolete test for conditional behavior built on the unconditional API is retired.

cases.description: A delayed root on a disconnected or superseded frontend cannot write a title or reclaim the binding
cases.setup: Create a private frontend binding and hold an unnamed root after its request has been observed. Trigger disconnect and activate the next connection before draining the old root.
cases.action: Release the old root after teardown, then bind a root on the new connection. Observe any attempted name writes and the final attachment.
cases.expected: The old connection grants neither a title write nor a binding. The current connection binds its own root and leaves the Codex name unchanged.

cases.description: A task label uses the Codex name only on a positively stamped HQ pane
cases.setup: Give an ordinary Codex pane the HQ working directory, a directory-derived supervisor role and a current same-home binding with a saved name. Add a verified stamped HQ case and a foreign-stamp case.
cases.action: Project the shared radar task before and after a matching stamp and a native user rename.
cases.expected: A matching HQ stamp and verified binding use the current saved name in the shared payload. An absent or foreign stamp keeps the ordinary label even when the directory implies a supervisor role. Existing role inference retains its own behavior.
